t: The Hephthalites, who called themselves Ebodalo on their coins, were militarily important from 450, when they defeated the Kidarites, to 560, when the First Turkic Khaganate and the Sasanian Empire destroyed them.
Peroz I fought three wars against them from 474: captured and ransomed twice, he was defeated and killed at the Battle of Herat in 484, and the Sasanians paid tribute until the 530s.
They were a tribal confederation of nomadic and settled communities who adopted the Bactrian language, took Sasanian coin designs, and ruled a largely Iranian population through local rulers.
dyk: Polyandry was the Hephthalites' most noted custom: brothers shared one wife, whose children belonged to the eldest, and the number of horns on a married woman's headdress showed how many husbands she had.
ev: The first Hephthalite embassy reaches the Chinese court of the Northern Wei; twenty-four embassies to China are recorded in all, the last in 558.
The Hephthalite king Akhshunwar helps Peroz I gain the Sasanian throne from his brother.
Peroz I begins three wars against his former allies; captured in the first two, he pays thirty mules loaded with silver drachms and leaves his son Kavad as a hostage.
At the Battle of Herat Peroz I is defeated and killed by the Hephthalite king Kun-khi; for two years the Hephthalites plunder and control the eastern Sasanian Empire.
A Hephthalite army defeats the Sasanian army of Balash and places Kavad I, who had lived four years among the Hephthalites, on the throne.
The Hephthalites capture Sughd, the capital of Sogdiana, and push north of Turfan to the Urumchi region in the Tarim Basin.
King Yilituo Yandai sends the first Hephthalite ambassador to the Southern Liang court, recorded in the Portraits of Periodical Offering of Liang.

The Turks of the First Turkic Khaganate and the Sasanians under Khosrow I defeat the Hephthalites after an eight-day battle near Qarshi, the Battle of Gol-Zarriun; the empire breaks into principalities.

f.capital: Probably Kunduz, known to al-Biruni as War-Waliz
f.predecessor: The Kidarites and the Alchon Huns in Bactria; the Rouran Khaganate, whose vassals the Hephthalites had been
f.successor: The First Turkic Khaganate and the Sasanian Empire of Khosrow I; Hephthalite principalities in Tokharistan, then the Tokhara Yabghus from 625
